cryptomatte: The Cryptomatte layers of the same EXRs, each id a colour weighted by its coverage: soft, anti-aliased edges where objects meet. Eldr names objects by prim path (`CryptoObject`) and materials by material path (`CryptoMaterial`), as Karma's Cryptomatte does.
![Cryptomatte: beauty, object and material mattes; Eldr and Karma CPU]({img}features/cryptomatte_mattes.jpg)
aovs: Its passes, Eldr ray traced (left of each pair) next to Karma CPU (right), from one EXR each: the diffuse and specular splits (`C<RD>.*L`, `C<RG>.*L`), the light refracted through the glass ball (`C<TG>.*L`), the two light groups (`C.*<L.'ceiling'>`, `C.*<L.'lamp'>`), normal (`ray:hitN`, shown as 0.5 + N / 2), depth (`ray:hitPz`, near is bright) and albedo (`CDA`). Eldr's light groups hold the group's direct light; Karma's add its bounced light.
![AOVs: beauty, diffuse, specular, transmission, light groups, normal, depth, albedo; Eldr and Karma CPU]({img}features/aovs_passes.jpg)
tiles: The tiled image (12 tiles of 512 pixels) against the whole image at once, and their difference ten times brighter: no seams along the tile edges, only a little noise and the chrome ball's reflection, which screen-space reflections find on screen in the whole image and the reflection probe supplies in a tile (traced reflections are the same either way).
![Tiled rendering: tiles, whole image and their difference]({img}features/tiles_whole.jpg)

The same scene (ray tracing off) at growing sizes with its `tiles` settings and 2048-pixel tiles (peak GPU memory above what was in use before the render, sampled by nvidia-smi). The screen-size buffers, about 170 bytes a pixel, stay at the tile's size; only the whole image's bloom, exposure and tonemapping grow with it, about 27 bytes a pixel. A whole 12000 × 12000 image would need about 24 GB.
